cautions: EVEN-HANDED TREATMENT is the defining control. Describe cultures, languages, religions, ethnic groups, and political positions NEUTRALLY and descriptively — no ethnocentrism, no ranking of cultures/religions, no advocacy. For contested political geography (disputed borders, sovereignty, geopolitical conflicts), present multiple perspectives and do NOT take a side on any specific territorial dispute; keep to general principles and widely-recognized facts, attributed.

DATE and ATTRIBUTE every demographic/development figure and verify it against the source. World population, growth rates, fertility, migration flows, refugee counts, urbanization rates, and HDI move constantly — attribute to the UN (WPP/UNHCR/UNDP), U.S. Census, or World Bank with the specific year (e.g., 'world population reached about 8 billion in November 2022, per the UN'). Never invent a statistic; prefer clearly-dated or rounded figures over stale precise ones.

Define terms with precision and guard the classic confusions: STATE vs NATION vs country (a state is a sovereign political territory; a nation is a people/cultural group; a nation-state aligns the two); ethnicity vs race vs nationality; population DISTRIBUTION (where people are) vs DENSITY (people per unit area, arithmetic vs physiological); migration PUSH vs PULL factors; and REFUGEE vs asylum-seeker vs internally displaced person (IDP) vs (economic) migrant — use the UNHCR/1951-Convention legal definitions exactly.

Treat models as models. The Demographic Transition Model is a STAGE-BASED GENERALIZATION grounded in the historical experience of industrializing European countries; present its stages accurately but note its limitations and that not every country follows it identically. Ravenstein's 'laws' of migration and the push-pull framework are useful frameworks, not deterministic laws — attribute them.

Handle SENSITIVE topics (forced displacement, refugees, ethnic conflict, colonialism's legacy) with accuracy and care, descriptively and without sensationalism; cite authoritative humanitarian sources (UNHCR/IOM) for figures. No individualized legal or immigration advice.

Attribute concepts and models to their sources where relevant (demographic transition; Ravenstein's laws of migration; central place theory or Von Thünen if agriculture is discussed; the 1951 Refugee Convention). Do not overstate any single figure as the sole originator of a broad idea.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic. Verify keys yourself from the file. Vary question stems across topics to avoid cross-topic near-duplicate flags.
